sections.h2: Who handles the paperwork when a Boynton Beach house sells?
sections.html:
Four offices hold pieces of your file. The county Property Appraiser describes the parcel, the county Tax Collector bills it, the Clerk and Comptroller keeps the recorded deed, and the city Building Department keeps permits. Knowing that split saves repeat phone calls once an offer arrives.

Owners pick between a listing, a private sale and a direct purchase from a cash buyer. Listings bring the widest audience along with open houses and punch lists. A direct purchase trades some price for fewer moving parts, and the closing date is yours to name.

  • Print the parcel record before anyone tours the house.
  • Request old permit files and final inspections from the city.
  • Ask each lender for a written payoff figure.

sections.h2: How does Boynton Beach's age shape a sale?
sections.html:
The place dates to a small settlement that became the Town of Boynton on April 14, 1920, per the city library's history page. A century of growth means a mix of mid-century blocks and newer subdivisions, and buyers price those very differently.

Older houses draw inspection requests. The city runs a permit history service holding building plans, site plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for addresses inside city limits. If a past owner added a screen room, replaced a roof or changed a panel, that file shows whether the work was closed out. An open permit is far easier to settle before a contract than during a buyer's inspection window.

The city's own page sends anyone asking about the year a home was built to the Property Appraiser, so expect a buyer's agent to look there first.

sections.h2: Will the new HB 803 permit exemption help me fix things before listing?
sections.html:
Sometimes. House Bill 803 took effect July 1, 2026 and created two permit exemptions for single family homes, and Boynton Beach built a request process in its online permitting portal.

The first covers small jobs valued under $7,500. You send the Building Department a written request with the contract or other proof of the work's scope and value, and staff either issue a written determination or tell you to apply for a permit. Splitting one project into pieces to stay under the cap is not allowed.

The city's page is blunt about limits. Structural, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and gas work still needs a permit whatever it costs, and so does any work on a property in a flood hazard area. Fences and driveways stay under the zoning code. The second exemption covers temporary flood panels or barriers installed by a state-certified contractor, and it also excludes flood hazard areas. For both, the city states it owes no legal duty to owners or successors for exempted work.

  • Listed as fine: interior trim, flooring, replacing cabinets, sinks and light fixtures, repairing drywall.
  • Listed as still permitted: moving sinks or water heaters, tub to shower conversions, windows, doors, shutters, garage or patio conversions.

Exempt work gets no city inspection, so keep receipts and photos to hand the buyer.

sections.h2: What city code problems turn up most in Boynton Beach listings?
sections.html:
The city's Common Code Violations page lists the repeat offenders, and most are cheap to correct before photos are taken.

  • Grass taller than nine inches, or dead sod that has not been replaced.
  • House numbers missing from the building itself; they must be at least four inches tall and contrast with the wall.
  • Peeling paint, damaged fascia, loose awnings or broken screen enclosures.
  • Inoperable or unregistered vehicles, appliances and household items stored outside.
  • Construction debris over three cubic yards, which needs a special pickup from Public Works.

Boats and recreational vehicles may sit on a driveway, in a carport or in the rear yard if a resident owns them, they are registered, and they are not under repair for more than seven days. Nobody may occupy a parked RV on private land unless zoning allows it.

The city also says no one may lease a residential unit without a business tax receipt and a certificate of use and occupancy for that unit. A landlord selling a rented house should confirm both were in place, since a buyer's lender or title agent may ask.

sections.h2: What is the Super Senior exemption, and does it affect a buyer?
sections.html:
Boynton Beach is one of only two cities named on the appraiser's exemption chart for a Super Senior exemption, the other being Delray Beach. It removes Boynton Beach's own levies, not the county, school or other bills.

To get it, an owner must meet the limited-income senior rules, have owned and lived in the home as a permanent residence for at least 25 years, and hold a property with market value under $250,000 at application. A long-time owner who has it should tell a buyer plainly, because the benefit belongs to the owner and does not pass with the house.

sections.h2: What still applies when the deed is signed?
sections.html:
Three statewide rules matter most. First, a land conveyance needs a signed writing with two witnesses, which may be taken over audio-video link. Second, the stamp tax runs seventy cents per hundred dollars here, and everyone named on the deed answers for it. Third, the Clerk collects it when the deed is recorded, with page-based fees under section 28.24.

Your closing agent should itemize all three on the draft settlement statement, so ask for it ahead of signing day. Switching to a quitclaim form does not avoid the tax when money or a mortgage is part of the deal.

sections.h2: What happens to my tax bill and homestead after a sale?
sections.html:
The bill for the year of sale is settled at the table, with the closing agent paying any open balance from proceeds. The buyer's own assessment resets to market value the January after closing.

Your accumulated cap savings follow you only if you file for portability when you claim a new Florida homestead. Renting out the home or moving away ends the exemption, so avoid placing a tenant while you wait to close. Owners with limited income may ask the Tax Collector about the deferral program, which uses Form DR-570.

faqs.q: Where can I see what work was permitted on my Boynton Beach house?
faqs.a: The city's permit history service holds plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for properties in city limits. Request your address file before you list, and use the Property Appraiser's record for the year built.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to swap kitchen cabinets before a sale?
faqs.a: Often not, under the city's HB 803 guidance, if the job is under $7,500 and involves no plumbing, electrical, structural, mechanical or gas work. You must file a written exemption request, and flood hazard area properties are excluded.

faqs.q: Can a Boynton Beach landlord sell a rented house?
faqs.a: Yes, but confirm the city business tax receipt and certificate of use and occupancy were in place for the unit. A buyer or title agent may ask for them.

faqs.q: Does the Super Senior exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. It is tied to the owner's 25 years of residence and income filing, so the next owner starts fresh and is assessed at full value after the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who collects the deed stamp tax on a Boynton Beach sale?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Clerk collects it at recording, and the sales contract decides which side pays. Ask your closing agent to show the figure on the draft settlement statement.
